reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key premises; claims about prior method limitations, impurity effects, decoupling feasibility, and expected accuracy improvement are entirely unsupported by the referenced literature.
premises: Lattice and electronic heat transport can be decoupled by explicit phonon-electron interaction and anharmonic scattering calculations
Oxygen impurities (~1 wt.%) significantly affect defect scattering and must be parametrized
Earlier Debye/DFT approaches assume perfect, defect-free crystals and conflate transport contributions
A 20% accuracy improvement over prior methods is achievable by capturing atomic-scale complexity
Lattice contribution dominates above 300 K while electronic contribution is comparable below 200 K in HfNbTaTiZr
